text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: SEV2 - continuous-batching perf cliff in us-west-2. 95p token latency > 2s for last 3m; errors (5xx) x4 on /v1/generate. Runbook: https://go/runbooks/cont-batch

alex: grabbing this — oncall alex. what zones? any customer escalations?

kevin: seeing spikes in us-west-2a/us-west-2b. cluster batcher pods showing queue depth oscillation + large KV cache growth.

maya: CS reports 3 paying customers hit with 500s intermittently, one on p95 request that timed out. CS ticket IDs: CS-4232, CS-4237.

alex: ok triage plan: 1) reduce incoming concurrency at router 2) lower max_microbatch to force smaller microbatches 3) disable prefetch if KV growth continues. anyone oppose?

kevin: +1. I can patch batcher config and run a canary in us-west-2a.

priya: logs look like prefetch loop: many prefix cache inserts then eviction storms. snippet: ```
2026-03-15T18:10:32Z batcher INFO prefetching 128 prefixes for model-ggml
2026-03-15T18:10:32Z kvcache WARN eviction_rate=0.87 free_slots=12
2026-03-15T18:10:33Z batcher ERROR microbatch timeout waiting for tokens=1/64
```

alex: that matches earlier prefetch-regression patterns. kevin can you set microbatch cap to 6 for canary? current is 16. command: `redwoodctl config set --service batcher --env prod --zone us-west-2a batch.max_microbatch=6`

kevin: running now. `redwoodctl` output: Deploy plan created -> canary to us-west-2a.

deploy-bot: Rollout started: service=batcher zone=us-west-2a param=batch.max_microbatch=6 id=rollout-4443210000-canary

alex: also set router backpressure to limit concurrent requests to 1200 in that zone: `kubectl apply -f -` ```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: router-backpressure
data:
  max_concurrent: "1200"
```

kevin: canary succeeded in us-west-2a. p95 latency dropped from 2.3s -> 420ms in that zone. KV cache insert rate down ~72%.

maya: CS note: customers reporting partial recovery, one still seeing timeouts. investigating whether they hit other zones.

priya: traces show request fanout > 12 for some long-tailed prompts; prefetch tries to fetch many prefixes concurrently and blows out the cache under high concurrency. likely regression from prefetch batching change in last release.

sam: copying release log: last deploy changed prefetch throttle gating (PR #9876). if root cause confirm, revert gate and add stricter limits.

alex: next step: disable prefetch globally as temporary mitigation and increase sampling for canary. command I propose: `redwoodctl config set --service batcher --env prod batcher.prefetch.enabled=false --force`

kevin: warning — disabling prefetch might increase latency for cold prefixes, but better than evictions and 5xx. I support.

alex: executing now for us-west-2 (all zones) as a quick fix. `redwoodctl rollout set --service batcher --env prod param=batcher.prefetch.enabled=false --scope=region:us-west-2`

deploy-bot: Rollout started: service=batcher region=us-west-2 param=batcher.prefetch.enabled=false id=rollout-4443210200-global
deploy-bot: Rollout success: rollout-4443210200-global -> 100% in us-west-2 (zones a,b,c)

kevin: after disabling prefetch region-wide: p95 latency down cluster-wide 60-80%, 5xx dropped to baseline. KV cache size trending down.

cs-bot: Notified affected customers: CS-4232, CS-4237, CS-4241. CS provided ETA 30m for dyed-in-the-wool verification.

alex: handing over to kevin to continue until stable. I'll go offline in 15m for patching but reachable. kevin, you're primary. :white_check_mark:

kevin: taking over. plan: 1) maintain prefetch disabled 2) push PR to revert gating change and add strict caps on concurrent prefetches 3) add telemetry for prefix fanout distribution 4) schedule postmortem.

priya: started a short-term hotfix PR to cap per-request prefetch concurrency: `prefetch.max_parallel_prefixes=8` — linking: https://go/repo/pull/9999

sam: please ensure we capture customer impact metrics and SLA exposure. set a follow-up with sales + CS.

maya: CS will draft communications after we confirm stability for 15m.

kevin: metrics stable for 8m since rollback. continuing to monitor. I'll escalate if we see any regressions.

alex: quick TL;DR for postmortem notes: root cause = prefetch batching/gating regression -> Thrash under high concurrency -> KV cache growth + eviction storms -> microbatch timeouts & request-level 5xx. Mitigations = lowered microbatch cap, router backpressure, disabled prefetch, canary rollouts; long-term = revert faulty change + add limits and better telemetry.

maya: adding bookmarks: /runbooks/cont-batch, /incidents/4443210000 for postmortem.

kevin: handing to sam for postmortem lead. marking this thread resolved when metrics stable for 30m.

sam: I'll take postmortem. please dump last 1h of cont-batch metrics to the incident channel and attach to postmortem doc. :eyes:

alex: thanks team — great coordination. closing watch but will re-open if any customer reports. :thumbsup:
